finding: Partial proof of item (3), extending the accepted continuous-input scalar formula to Haar L² kernels and inputs on the actual idèle class group of every number field. At each x, both products φ(g) f(g⁻¹x) and φ(x/y) f(y) are integrable and their integrals against the same class Haar agree. The kernel integral at each x is independent of a.e. representatives of both factors, is bounded by the product of the Haar L² norms, and obeys the norm-one character law if the input obeys it a.e. for each fixed subgroup element. Convergence in L²(ν) for ν dominating class Haar gives uniform scalar convergence on the entire class group; the client checks domination for the source symmetric squared weight including s=0. The unchanged Theorems.IdeleClassConvolutionKernel gives support-gap and diagonal vanishing for the original kernel test (earlier receipt at 0c1d5fcef0853fb9f213253b7f60dbd15173c8f9). This update is not the bounded weighted output action or identification with the actual completed middle isotype. It does not use extension by zero, change the Haar scale, or establish any operator trace, quotient descent, or spectral comparison.
retry: Supply the actual general completed weighted norm-one isotype and density of its source tests for the squared norm of p. 11 / (9.2.2.34), and a bounded inverse-left action into that weighted model agreeing with the source test integral and preserving the isotype. Compare its weighted L² output limits a.e. with the uniform scalar kernel limits proved here. The accepted rational-radial action does not provide those general bridges.
